title: Founders, fixers and the grandson
lede: Ages and titles are as given in the press at the time. Later careers are left out where we have no source.

people.name: Sam Battistone Sr.
people.text: Worked as a busboy, waiter and manager in California restaurants before opening the first Sambo’s with Bohnett in 1957. Resigned as chairman at 69 under pressure from creditors, and stayed on as a director.[^2][^18]
people.later: Sued by the company’s new management in 1981, with Bohnett and 26 others, for $100M. The outcome of that suit is not in our sources. The Los Angeles Times says he died in 1991.[^6][^7][^18]

people.name: F. Newell “Bo” Bohnett
people.text: A restaurant-equipment salesman and former Marine Corps pilot who supplied the second half of the name.[^17][^29]
people.later: Moved to Hawaii in 1968 and bought a 107,000-acre ranch there in 1972. Died on January 1, 2017, aged 93.[^29]

people.name: Sam D. Battistone
people.text: The founder’s son, who cooked beside his father at the 1957 opening and became chairman at 39. He was also one of the founding owners of the New Orleans Jazz basketball team, which he later moved to Salt Lake City.[^2][^17]
people.later: Bought the Santa Barbara restaurant back from Vicorp after selling the Utah Jazz in 1985–86.[^17]

people.name: Daniel R. Shaughnessy
people.text: Head of the Motel 6 management team that City Investing’s affiliate installed at Sambo’s. He declined to describe his strategy: “In March, we’ll have something to talk about.”[^2]

people.name: George T. Scharffenberger
people.text: Led the New York conglomerate that owned Motel 6 and, through GDV, took 34% of Sambo’s by 1980.[^2][^6]

people.name: Arthur K. Dowd
people.text: The voice of the company through the renamings, the closings and the filing. He said the Chapter 11 petition would “have absolutely no effect on the company’s operations.”[^5][^10]

people.name: Charles J. McLaughlin
people.text: The trustee who announced the court-approved sale of 166 restaurants to Vicorp in August 1984.[^14]

people.name: Chad Stevens
people.role: Owner of the last restaurant from 1998
people.text: Battistone Sr.’s grandson. He planned a revival of the chain in 1998, kept the name for 22 years and replaced it with his own in July 2020.[^18][^24][^26]
people.later: Still runs the restaurant as Chad’s, according to its website.[^28]

people.name: Rashelle Monet
people.text: The Santa Barbara resident whose petition and public comment to the city council led to the change. She helped cover the sign from a crane.[^23][^24]
